To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number and average size of echo chambers, opinion-based communities and modularity of social network predict changes in vaccination uptake and disease dynamics.
the number and average size of echo chambers in social networks are good predictors of critical transitions in vaccination and disease dynamics.
echo chambers and opinion based communities are good EWS for changes in vaccine uptake in social networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spread of infectious diseases in social networks.
the study of the interplay between the spread of infectious diseases and the dynamics of social contact networks.
the development of new mathematical and computational methods for studying complex systems, and in particular for understanding the dynamics of networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

echo chambers and opinion based communities can be considered as EWS of changes in vaccination rates and infectious disease spread, but the EWS efficacy decreases with the strength of the social norms in the population.
the number and size of opinion-based echo chambers in social networks are early warnings of a sudden shift in vaccine uptake and infectious disease spread.
echo chambers are early warning signals of changes in the dynamics of a disease model, and are a good predictor of changes in the infection dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of the network, and not the network itself, is the key to understanding the dynamics of a system.
the social structure of a network, as represented by the number of echo chambers and their size, is an early indicator of a change in the health of a population.
we have shown that the structure of social networks is an early warning signal for the transition to the endemic state of an epidemiological model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
echo chambers and other measures of community structure in a social epidemiological network provide early warnings of changes in vaccination rates and health outcomes.
social networks can be used as a tool to predict the future.
echo chambers and opinion based communities are useful EWS for predicting changes in the spread of disease.
